definitions.explanation: A written or printed representation of music using musical notation; the physical sheets or document containing the notes to be performed.

examples.japanese: {譜面|ふめん}を{見|み}ながら{演奏|えんそう}した。
examples.english: I played while reading the sheet music.

examples.japanese: この{曲|きょく}の{譜面|ふめん}を{持|も}っていますか。
examples.english: Do you have the sheet music for this piece?

examples.japanese: プロの{演奏家|えんそうか}は{譜面|ふめん}を{見|み}なくても{弾|ひ}けることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Professional musicians can often play without looking at the sheet music.

notes:
USAGE:
{譜面|ふめん} is commonly used among musicians and in music education. It refers to the physical document or display of musical notation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {譜面|ふめん}を{読|よ}む (to read sheet music)
- {譜面|ふめん}{台|だい} (music stand)
- {譜面|ふめん}{通|どお}りに{弾|ひ}く (to play exactly as written)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {譜面|ふめん}: the physical score/sheet music (practical, musician's term)
- {楽譜|がくふ}: musical score (slightly more formal/general)
- スコア: full orchestral score (from English "score")
